newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends at new high, fueled by profit news.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends at new high, fueled by profit news.

text.p: A strong quarterly profit report from Eastman Kodak Co helped push U.S. blue chips to a record closing high on Thursday, despite a mid-session inflation scare that rattled the jittery stock market.
The Dow industrials ended up 38 points, or 0.57 percent, to 6765, eclipsing the record high of 6762 set on Tuesday.

Blue chips fought back late in the day after inflation comments from a Federal Reserve governor sparked a mid-session reversal that erased a 55-point advance. "There's a lot of volatility," said Bob Dickey, Dain Bosworth technical analyst.
Kodak, the top gainer among the Dow 30, rose 4-1/4 to 85-1/2 after its earnings beat Wall Street expectations and it raised its quarterly dividend.

The Nasdaq market also got a boost from earnings news, led by Sun Microsystems Inc, which rose 2-13/16 to 31-1/16 after reporting late Wednesday a 41 percent profit rise in its latest quarter and record revenues.
The Nasdaq composite finished up almost seven points to 1340, just shy of its record closing high of 1346 set Tuesday.

The Dow shot up over 50 points in early dealing, but tumbled into negative ground around midday after comments by Fed governor Laurence Meyer that he saw a risk of higher inflation in the U.S. economy.
Both the stock and bond markets have been on edge, reacting to any news or economic data that might tip the Fed toward raising interest rates.

"This market has got a bit of a case of nerves," said Michael LaTronica, director of research at Gruntal. "But that's a symptom of a market that has come as far as this one has in the last couple of years."
But while stocks recovered, bonds stayed weak. The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was off 14/32 in late trading, its yield rising to 6.83 percent from Wednesday's close at 6.79 percent.

Traders and analysts expected more whipsaw action in coming sessions on Wall Street as the market tries to absorb institutional investor cash flows, corporate earnings news and continued inflation concerns.
"It's just a real split market because of all the different cross currents that are occurring right now," Dickey said.
Digital Equipment Corp rose 2-1/2 to 36-3/4 after the company's second quarter earnings topped analysts' mean estimate of $0.10 a share. The company earned $0.15 a share, down from $0.91 a year ago.
General Electric Co posted fourth quarter profits this morning that matched analysts' estimates. Its shares ended off 1-3/8 at 101-1/2.

Pharmaceutical company Pfizer Inc posted fourth quarter results that matched Wall Street expectations and the company expects double-digit growth in sales and net income in 1997. The stock rose 3/8 to 87-1/4.

Value Health Inc, a provider of specialty health-care services, rose 1-3/4 to 22, after it and Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp, the nation's largest for-profit provider of health care services, announced a $1.3 billion merger deal late Wednesday. Columbia/HCA ended off one at 39-1/4.

Georgia-Pacific shares fell 1/4 to 77-1/8 after the company said fourth quarter profits were hurt by a collapse in prices for most of its products. Its fourth quarter earnings were $0.02 a share. The Wall Street consensus estimate was $0.38, according to First Call.

Apple Computer Inc dropped 1/2 to 16-3/4 after the computer maker posted after the market's close Wednesday a $0.96 a share loss in its latest quarter and warned investors it did not expect to report a profit until September. Analysts at Lehman Brothers, Goldman Sachs downgraded their ratings on Apple's shares.
The S&P 500 index rose 2.55 to 769.75, a record.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
